aliases: Sample 3 of the three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys

source.reason: The arc-cladding process and its parameter window are the fabrication route used for the three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si coatings (Samples 1–3), described in the coating-preparation text and in the 'Parameters of cladding' table.

processing_steps_notes.value: Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si coating (Sample 3) prepared by arc cladding using wire of the optimized element content as feedstock onto an ASTM A36 steel substrate (300 mm × 120 mm × 40 mm); equipment IDEALARC DC-1000 (Lincoln Electric, America). Cladding parameters: current 440 ~ 600 A, voltage 30 ~ 32 V, cladding speed 24 m/h, interlayer temperature 380 ~ 410 °C, wire feed speed 76.8 m/h.

source.reason: The XRD phase description (Sample 3 main phase Fe-Cr-Ni, peak indexing and right-shift relative to standard Fe) and the solid-solution formation criteria (with Sample 3's δr and ΔHmix from Table 6) pertain to this sample.

overall_structure.value: Main phase is the Fe-Cr-Ni solid-solution phase; XRD shows a single dominant (1 1 0) reflection with weak (2 0 0) and (2 1 1) reflections, and the peaks are shifted to higher 2θ relative to standard Fe (lattice distortion). Solid-solution phase formation is consistent with the criteria δr < 0.066 and −11.6 < ΔHmix < 3.2 kJ/mol (Sample 3: δr = 0.0335, ΔHmix = −0.451 kJ/mol).

crystal_structure.value: bcc-type Fe-Cr(±Ni) solid-solution (XRD reflections indexed (1 1 0), (2 0 0), (2 1 1); text states Cr atoms randomly substituted Fe in a lattice with (1 0 0), (2 0 0), (2 1 1) peaks)

lattice_distortion.value: Diffraction peak of the alloy shifted to higher 2θ relative to standard Fe, attributed to the atomic radius differences between Cr, Ni and Fe.

source.reason: The Vicker's microhardness measurement (indenter, load and holding time) and the experimental microhardness value reported for Sample 3 constitute the property record for this sample.

other_conditions.value: Vicker's microhardness measured on the coating with a microhardness indenter; load 1 kg, holding time 20 s.

source.reason: Fig. 9 reports the experimental microhardness of Sample 3 as 424 HV in the predicted-vs-experimental bar chart, and the citing text states the microhardness prediction model was validated by experiments; the measurement method is described in the characterization section.
Fig. 9 and the citing text give Sample 3's predicted (415 HV) versus experimental (424 HV) microhardness with a 2.09 % error, i.e. the model-validation performance of this sample.

comparison_metric.value: Error between ML-predicted microhardness (415 HV) and experimental microhardness (424 HV) for Sample 3 = 2.09 %

source.reason: The XRD technique, instrument/setup and measurement conditions are stated in the characterization section, and the Sample 3 phase identification and peak shift are given in the XRD results and figure.

instrument_or_setup.value: SmartLab SE, Rigaku, Japan, with Cu Kα radiation, working voltage 40 kV and current 40 mA

purpose.value: Phase analysis of the coating; identification of the main phase and detection of lattice distortion.

key_findings.value: Sample 3 main phase is the Fe-Cr-Ni phase with diffraction peaks indexed (1 1 0), (2 0 0) and (2 1 1) (text: 100, 200, 211); the (1 1 0) peak is shifted to higher 2θ relative to the standard Fe reference, indicating lattice distortion from atomic radius differences between Cr, Ni and Fe.

source.reason: The Vicker's microhardness instrument and test conditions are described in the characterization section and the measured value for Sample 3 is given in Fig. 9.

instrument_or_setup.value: Microhardness indenter HVS-1000A, Laizhou Huayin Testing Instrument Co., Ltd., China

purpose.value: Measure the microhardness of the coating.

key_findings.value: Experimental microhardness of Sample 3 = 424 HV (predicted 415 HV, error 2.09 %).

source.reason: The ML model (SVR + modified solid solution strengthening theory) is the inverse-design/validation computation that produced and validated the composition and microhardness of the Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys including Sample 3.

simulation_method.value: Support vector regression (SVR) machine-learning model combined with a modified solid solution strengthening theory, with hyperparameters optimized by Bayesian optimization and ten-fold cross-validation

potential_model_or_database.value: MatWeb materials information repository dataset (173 data points collected; 98 expanded to 192 by CGANs; 117 points used as validation set)

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Input key features {G, δEc, DEc}; output microhardness. SVR hyperparameters: C = 4.98, cache_size = 118.85, coef0 = 0.63, degree = 4, epsilon = 1.87 × 10^-4, gamma = 3.57 × 10^-2, kernel = ploy, tol = 1.22 × 10^-3.

validation_against_experiment.value: R² = 0.89 and RMSE = 0.31 on the 117-point validation set; for Sample 3 predicted microhardness 415 HV vs experimental 424 HV (2.09 % error).

equation_role.value: Predict the solid solution strengthening contribution to microhardness: Δσsss = Z·M·G·δEc·DEc

model_note.value: M (Taylor factor) = 3.06 for both FCC and BCC structures; Z is a fitting parameter with value 0.0056.

unmapped_findings: Sample 3 (mass percentages from Table 6): C 0.15, Si 0.5, Mn 1.5, Cr 5.2, S 0, Ni 1.2, P 0, Fe 89.7, Mo 1.5, V 0.25, W 0; δr = 0.0335 and ΔHmix = −0.451 kJ/mol.
Sample 3 satisfies the solid-solution formation criteria δr < 0.066 (here 0.0335) and −11.6 < ΔHmix < 3.2 kJ/mol (here −0.451 kJ/mol), consistent with its solid-solution Fe-Cr-Ni phase.

Sample 3 is one of three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys fabricated by arc cladding to experimentally verify the microhardness prediction accuracy of the ML model; its ML-predicted microhardness (415 HV) is closest to but slightly higher than the measured value (424 HV) within the 2.09 % error.
